overview: Bulgaria is a country in south-eastern Europe, on the western shore of the Black Sea. Its capital and largest city is Sofia. Bulgaria was part of the Ottoman Empire for about five centuries until 1878, and later a communist state until 1990. It joined NATO in 2004 and the European Union in 2007. It uses the Cyrillic alphabet, which was developed in the medieval Bulgarian Empire.

geography.text: The Balkan Mountains run across the middle of Bulgaria, with the wide Danube plain to the north, where the Danube forms most of the border with Romania. In the south-west the Rila and Pirin mountains rise higher still, and Musala in the Rila range is the highest peak in the Balkans. In the east, Bulgaria has a coastline of beaches and resorts on the Black Sea.

history.text: The First Bulgarian Empire was founded in 681 and became one of the great powers of medieval Europe. The Ottomans ruled Bulgaria from the late 1300s until 1878. After the Second World War it became a communist state allied with the Soviet Union, and it moved to democracy in 1990.

events.title: First Bulgarian Empire
events.text: Khan Asparukh founds a Bulgarian state on the Danube.

events.title: Cyrillic alphabet
events.text: Scholars in the Bulgarian Empire develop the Cyrillic script.

events.title: Ottoman conquest
events.text: The last Bulgarian kingdom falls to the Ottomans.

events.title: Liberation
events.text: Bulgaria becomes self-governing after a Russian victory over the Ottomans.

events.title: Joins the EU
events.text: Bulgaria becomes a member of the European Union.

government.text: Bulgaria is a parliamentary republic. Voters elect a 240-member National Assembly, which chooses the Prime Minister and government. The President is elected directly every five years. Bulgaria joined NATO in 2004 and the European Union in 2007, and it has had many elections in recent years as parties struggled to form stable governments.

economy.text: Bulgaria has one of the lower average incomes in the European Union but has grown steadily. Its economy includes IT and outsourcing, manufacturing, farming and tourism on the Black Sea coast and in its ski resorts. Bulgaria grows much of the world's rose oil, used in perfume.

culture.text: The Cyrillic alphabet was developed in the First Bulgarian Empire, and Bulgarians celebrate it every 24 May. Bulgarian folk music is known for its unusual rhythms and powerful choirs. Bulgarians nod to mean no and shake their heads to mean yes.

items.title: Rila Monastery
items.text: A colourful monastery in the mountains, founded in the 900s.

items.title: Rose Valley
items.text: Rose fields near Kazanlak produce oil for perfumes around the world.

items.title: Martenitsa
items.text: Red-and-white threads worn on 1 March to welcome spring.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport; Bulgaria reached the World Cup semi-finals in 1994, led by Hristo Stoichkov. Bulgaria has also been strong in weightlifting, wrestling and rhythmic gymnastics.

items.text: Bulgaria reached the World Cup semi-finals in the United States.

items.title: Rhythmic gymnastics
items.text: Bulgaria won Olympic gold in the group event in 2021.

didYouKnow: Bulgaria's Rose Valley produces a large share of the world's rose oil, used in perfume.
Yoghurt bacteria Lactobacillus bulgaricus is named after Bulgaria.

keyPeople.name: Vasil Levski
keyPeople.text: Fought for Bulgarian freedom from Ottoman rule; a national hero.

keyPeople.name: John Atanasoff
keyPeople.text: American inventor of an early electronic computer, of Bulgarian descent.
